hooks.text: Persistent myths claim Earth blocks the Sun to change the Moon's shape.
The Moon’s changing phases have nothing to do with Earth’s shadow.
Why do we see a crescent Moon if Earth isn't in the way?

title: The Ancient Myth About the Moon’s Shape
description: Discover why the changing phases of the Moon are actually a trick of perspective rather than Earth's shadow.

beats.text: Persistent myths claim Earth blocks the Sun to change the Moon's shape.
beats.visual: Moon phases diagram showing Sun illumination by NASA

beats.text: This cycle has been tracked for nearly 10,000 years at the Warren Field site in Scotland.
beats.visual: Warren Field archaeological site pits in Scotland

beats.text: The ancient pit alignment beats any other formal record of human timekeeping ever discovered.
beats.visual: Illustration of the Mesolithic pit alignment at Warren Field

beats.text: Despite these millennia of observation, many people still misunderstand the physical trick behind these phases.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Earth casting a shadow toward the Moon

beats.text: The Sun constantly illuminates half the Moon, but our viewpoint shifts as it orbits Earth every 27.3 days.
beats.visual: Lunar orbit geometry diagram showing Sun and Earth

beats.text: We aren't seeing Earth’s shadow; we are watching the boundary between lunar day and night from different angles.
beats.visual: Telescope view of the Moon terminator line showing crater shadows

beats.text: Outside of rare eclipses occurring twice a year, Earth's shadow never actually touches the Moon.
beats.visual: Total lunar eclipse blood moon by NASA
queries: Total lunar eclipse blood moon NASA

beats.text: The visual illusion remains convincing to this day.

better_than_last: Applied the 'record' structure by using the Warren Field calendar as the historical anchor before transitioning to the modern physical explanation and the eclipse surprise.
